subject: Food Science
title: Sugar Preservation
description: A micro-lesson that makes Sugar Preservation usable.

hook.text: Jam lasts over a year in your pantry. Remove the sugar and the same fruit molds in three days.

buildup.text: Like salt, sugar reduces water activity by binding free water molecules. At 65% sugar concentration, most microbes die.

discovery.text: Jams, jellies, candied fruit, and condensed milk all exploit sugar's ability to starve microbes of available water.

twist.text: Osmophilic yeasts survive in high-sugar zones. That's why opened jam eventually molds—sugar dilutes on the surface.

climax.text: Traditional preserves used equal weights of fruit and sugar—50% concentration. Modern low-sugar jams need refrigeration.

punchline.text: Sugar binds water so microbes can't drink. Sweet preservation, literally.

quiz.question: Why do low-sugar jams need refrigeration?
options: Less sugar means higher water activity—microbes can still grow
